source_text: Aut certe, quia hoc in lege non potest inveniri, acquiesce, impudentissime, de eo peccato loqui Apostolum, quod imitatione trahitur, voluntate committitur, ratione arguitur, lege ostenditur, aequitate punitur.
pass_a_gloss: Or certainly, because this cannot be found in the law, acquiesce, most shameless man, that the Apostle speaks about that sin which is drawn by imitation, committed by will, convicted by reason, shown by law, punished by equity.

lemmas.lexica: LS imitatio; Blaise moral copying vs generation of sin
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Or else, since this cannot be found in the law, agree, most shameless man, that the apostle is speaking of the sin acquired by imitation, committed by will, exposed by reason, disclosed by law, and punished by justice.

choices.why: Julian's Rom 5:12 reading: sin passes by copying Adam's example, not by generation/seed.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
